correctness.rationale: Over C the gradient is 4 z_i(S+t z_i^2), so for t nonzero every singular projective point has k nonzero coordinates of the same square and t=-k. Each such point lies on the fibre; the support/sign count is binomial(4,k) 2^(k-1) and signed permutations act transitively. In a chart with one supported coordinate set to 1, at the all-positive representative the affine Hessian splits into 8(J_(k-1)-kI) and 4k I_(4-k). Both blocks are invertible when present. The resulting finite singular locus rules out repeated factors and reducibility, and gives normality by the hypersurface Cohen–Macaulay property and regularity in codimension one. At zero the equation is the square of a smooth quadric, and the Fermat member at infinity is smooth. At each node Q takes the value k after normalization, giving order one on its local discriminant branch; locally the different nodes contribute one factor each. The degree 108 of the quartic discriminant then leaves order 68 at zero. The explicit resultant specialization in the originality assessment independently gives all orders without using transversality. The submitted verification code was not executed.

evidence: Normalize the partials to P_i=z_i S+t z_i^3. Their first, second, third and fourth index divided differences, up to sign, are xS+t x^3, S+t(x^2+xy+y^2), t(x+y+z), and t.

The partitions (4),(3,1),(2,2),(2,1,1) have weights 1,4,3,6. Their respective specialized resultants, up to nonzero constants, are (t+4), t^2(t+1)(t+3)(t+4), t^2(t+2)^2(t+4), and t^8(t+2)(t+3)^2. In the binary stages use S=a x^2+b y^2, factor P_1=x(S+t x^2), and note that the second divided difference differs from S+t x^2 by t y(x+y). In the ternary stage extract t^6 from the linear input and set z=-x-y before applying the same binary calculation with S=3x^2+2xy+2y^2.
The constant fourth divided difference has exponent m_0=108-(1+4*5+3*5+6*11)=6. Multiplication gives t^68(t+1)^4(t+2)^12(t+3)^16(t+4)^8, exactly.
